title: Nivolumab for Recurrent Squamous-Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (CheckMate 141)
authors: Ferris RL, Blumenschein G Jr, Fayette J, Guigay J, et al.

pico.label: Population
pico.text: 361 adults with recurrent or metastatic squamous-cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, pharynx or larynx that had progressed within 6 months of platinum chemotherapy, ECOG 0 to 1. Recruited June 2014 to August 2015. 91.4% had previous radiotherapy and 54.5% had two or more previous lines of systemic therapy.

pico.label: Intervention
pico.text: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity (n = 240).

pico.label: Comparator
pico.text: Investigator's choice of weekly single-agent methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab (n = 121; given to 46, 52 and 13 patients).

pico.label: Outcome
pico.text: Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival and objective response. Exploratory: outcomes by PD-L1 expression and p16 status, and patient-reported quality of life.

bottom: In platinum-refractory disease, nivolumab extended median overall survival from 5.1 to 7.5 months (HR 0.70) and doubled 1-year survival from 16.6% to 36.0%, with fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events (13.1% versus 35.1%). The result comes from a planned interim analysis with a median follow-up of 5.1 months. Only 13.3% of patients responded and progression-free survival was not improved, so the benefit is concentrated in a minority.

appraisal.heading: The question
appraisal.text: Patients whose head and neck cancer progresses within 6 months of platinum had a median survival of around 6 months and no treatment that prolonged life. Early-phase data suggested PD-1 blockade had activity. This trial asked whether nivolumab improves survival over the single agents then in use.

appraisal.heading: Who and where
appraisal.text: An international academic and industry collaboration, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb, which designed the trial with the academic authors and paid for medical writing support.

appraisal.heading: Design and methods
appraisal.text: Open-label phase 3 trial with 2:1 randomisation, stratified by previous cetuximab. The sample of 360 patients and 278 deaths gave 90% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.667, with one interim analysis at 70% of events under an O'Brien-Fleming boundary. Efficacy was analysed by intention to treat, with response assessed by investigators. Progression-free survival and response were tested hierarchically only if survival was positive. PD-L1 and p16 analyses were exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity. Nivolumab could be continued beyond progression.

appraisal.heading: Results
appraisal.text: At the interim analysis there were 133 deaths (55.4%) with nivolumab and 85 (70.2%) with standard therapy. Median overall survival 7.5 months (95% CI 5.5 to 9.1) versus 5.1 months (4.0 to 6.0); HR 0.70 (97.73% CI 0.51 to 0.96; P = 0.01). One-year survival 36.0% versus 16.6%. Against each comparator the hazard ratio was 0.64 for methotrexate, 0.82 (0.53 to 1.28) for docetaxel and 0.47 (0.22 to 1.01) for cetuximab. Progression-free survival HR 0.89 (0.70 to 1.13), median 2.0 versus 2.3 months, with 6-month rates of 19.7% versus 9.9%. Response rate 13.3% versus 5.8%. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events 13.1% versus 35.1%. Median treatment duration was 1.9 months in both arms.

appraisal.heading: Strengths
points: Overall survival as the primary endpoint in an open-label trial, which removes assessment bias from the main result.
A prespecified interim boundary that was crossed, with intention-to-treat analysis.
A comparator that reflected real practice at the time.
Less severe toxicity than chemotherapy, with quality of life maintained on nivolumab while it declined on standard therapy.

appraisal.heading: Weaknesses and bias
points: Median follow-up was 5.1 months. The durable tail that defines immunotherapy could not be measured in this report.
The median gain is 2.4 months and 87% of patients did not respond. Most patients derive no benefit.
The survival curves separate late and the progression-free curves cross. The hazards are not proportional, so the hazard ratio is an average that hides early equivalence or harm.
The standard arm had more patients aged 65 or over and more never-smokers, and 10 of its 121 patients never received treatment.
The advantage over docetaxel alone is not statistically secure.
PD-L1 status was evaluable in only 72% of patients, and the biomarker analyses were exploratory.
Open label, with investigator-assessed response and patient-reported outcomes.
Sponsor involvement in design and writing. Eligibility was limited to ECOG 0 to 1.

appraisal.heading: What the abstract does not tell you
appraisal.text: That this is an interim analysis with a 97.73% confidence interval. That the hazards were non-proportional. That treatment lasted a median of under 2 months in both arms. That the comparison with docetaxel, the most active comparator, crosses 1. That PD-L1 could not be assessed in more than a quarter of patients. The Kaplan-Meier curves overlap for the first 3 months, and by 12 months only 24 nivolumab and 5 standard therapy patients remain at risk, so the 1-year survival rates rest on few patients; in PD-L1 below 1% the survival curves overlap throughout (HR 0.89). The quality-of-life plots come from the 129 patients who returned questionnaires. The subgroup hazard ratios by PD-L1 and p16 status are in Table 2 and the supplementary appendix and are not reproduced in this appraisal.

appraisal.heading: How it changed practice
appraisal.text: This was the first trial to show a survival benefit after platinum failure in head and neck cancer. It led to the licensing of nivolumab for this indication and made PD-1 blockade the standard second-line treatment. It also set up the first-line question answered by KEYNOTE-048. For an MDT today its main relevance is for patients who relapse soon after platinum-based chemoradiotherapy and have not yet had immunotherapy.
